rules.padlock: A padlock is a place in a Source column (#colour), never tapped, never in a slot; while on top it blocks its column. Its key lies on the board in a 2x2 hole without tiles (no work). The key leaves the board only when BOTH (a) its padlock is the top of its column and (b) an ant reaches the key (hole connected to the cleared area / an ant arrives); it flies over the slot row to the padlock (no slot used) and the padlock vanishes 0.25-1 s after the key starts. A key reachable earlier stays on the board (L194 cyan, L165 cyan, L113, L50 cyan); a padlock reaching the top before its key is reachable waits (11-97 s observed). Then the capsules below move up.
rules.door: Wooden crate with a coloured gem and N, covering a rectangle (4x4 to 12x13). N decreases by 1 for every unit of work of the gem's colour completed anywhere (a tile of that colour eaten, or a unit fed to a jar of that colour); it is not fed and consumes no work; it does not need to be reachable. At 0 it vanishes and the tiles under it (ordinary tiles, any colours, holding capsule work) become available. It blocks paths while closed (tiles under it are not eaten).
rules.chocolate: Chocolate bar with N covering a rectangle: N decreases by 1 for every unit of work of any colour (tiles and jar feeding); all bars on a board count down together; consumes no work; at 0 it vanishes and uncovers ordinary tiles holding capsule work.
rules.counter: Small 2x2 jar with N (L358 x3 '100', L290 '100', L192 60/80/90, L185 '90'): a consumer. Ants of its colour deliver units to it, each unit -1 and taken from a pod's count; no tile under it; at 0 it vanishes leaving 2x2 empty cells, or shows a next layer (L290: cyan 100 then orange 4). Feeding started at once even for jars inside an intact board (L192 80, L290), so whether a path is needed is unknown. L67's '100' and L266's '20'/'50' are not jars: chocolate bars and crates.
rules.hidden: Grey ? tile: an ordinary tile of a hidden colour that holds work; it shows its colour once one of its 4 neighbours is empty, and only then can ants of that colour eat it; before that it is a wall (L34).
